content: For individuals with diabetes, physical activity should be progressively increased in terms of intensity, frequency, and/or duration. The goal is to achieve at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity exercise per week. This could include activities such as brisk walking at a pace of approximately 7 km/h for at least 25 minutes per session. Alternatively, shorter durations of vigorous-intensity exercise or interval training, totaling around 75 minutes per week, can also provide significant benefits. Adults with diabetes are encouraged to incorporate resistance training exercises, such as using free weights or resistance bands, into their routine 2 to 3 times per week on non-consecutive days. While heavier resistance training may lead to improved blood glucose control and increased strength, even low-intensity resistance exercises can contribute to better strength, balance, and overall daily functional abilities.
